units: <cite ref="Taanit 27b:11">Taan. 27ᵇ</cite> <he>כל פ׳ דלא פסקיה וכ׳</he> you must not divide a verse which Moses has not divided, i.e. in reading you must not stop in the middle of a verse; <cite ref="Megillah 22a:5">Meg. 22ᵃ</cite>.

<cite ref="Megillah 25a:12">Ib. 25ᵃ</cite> <he>דאמר פ׳ פ׳ וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>פ׳</he> only) when he recites each verse (of the Sh’mʿa) and repeats it; <cite ref="Berakhot 33b:29">Ber. 33ᵇ</cite> <he>פְּסוּקָה פסוקה</he>.
<cite ref="Chagigah 15a:13">Ḥag. 15ᵃ</cite> sq. <he>אמר ליה פסוק לי פְּסוּקָךְ</he> he said to a child, tell me thy verse; a. fr.—Pl. <he>פְּסוּקִין</he>, <he>פְּסוּקַיָּא</he>, <he>פְּסוּקֵי</he>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:7:9">Y. M. Kat. III, 83ᵇ</cite> bot. (expl. <he>דלתות</he>, <cite ref="Jeremiah 36:23">Jer. XXXVI, 23</cite>) <he>תלת ארבע פ׳</he> (ed. Krot. <cite ref="Q01314"><he>פְּסִיקָן</he></cite>) three or four verses.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 30a:13">Kidd. 30ᵃ</cite> <he>פ׳ מיהא ליתו וכ׳</he> let us bring up the Torah and count the verses; <he>בפ׳ נמי לא בקיאינן</he> we (Babylonians) know not even the division of verses.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 30a:13">Ib.</cite> <he>במערבא פסקי ליה … תלתא פ׳</he> in Palestine they divided this verse (<cite ref="Exodus 19:9">Ex. XIX, 9</cite>) into three verses; a. fr.
